result.title: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting
result.summary: 4D occupancy forecasting predicts the 3D semantic occupancy of a driving scene seconds ahead. Over a few seconds, the scene changes little while the vehicle moves, so most of the space ahead has already been seen. Sorting the future into unchanged, changed, and unseen space, we find that current camera-based world models fall short on the unchanged part: they fail to hold on to what they have already seen, rather than to forecast what will change. We therefore make what the model has seen its state. PersistWorld streams camera frames into a persistent 3D world state anchored in the scene, writing each frame once instead of rebuilding the state from past frames. The state is learned end to end with the forecast, and an evolver predicts it at any queried time along the ego trajectory. On Occ3D-nuScenes, PersistWorld raises the IoU of the best camera-based world model by 19 points at 1-3 s and by 18 to 24 points up to 8 s, while running more than twice as fast. Code and models: https://github.com/wangzian828/PersistWorld. Project page: https://wangzian828.github.io/PersistWorld

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PersistWorld，将车载相机帧流式写入一个场景锚定的持久 3D 世界状态（每帧只写一次而非由历史帧重建），并用与预测端到端联合学习的 evolver 在自车轨迹上任意查询时刻预测该状态，用于 4D 语义占用预测；作者指出相机世界模型的主要短板在于守住已见空间，而非预测变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「状态一次写入、锚定于场景、按查询时刻演化」的持久状态设计，可能与 LVR 中如何保留视觉证据、避免内部状态信息坍缩以及状态更新与动态计算的问题相关，可供核查；但任务是驾驶占用预测，迁移性尚待确认。
